title: Nvidia's China AI-chip share falls to 34% as Huawei reaches 28%
content:
Nvidia’s share of China’s data-center AI accelerator market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, while Huawei reached 28%, according to an IDC report seen by Reuters. US export restrictions constrained Nvidia’s supplies as Chinese chipmakers expanded shipments.
Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China between January and June, down 44% from a year earlier. Huawei shipped 572,000, compared with more than 300,000 in the same period last year. The chips are used to train AI models and run inference.
Alibaba’s T-Head accounted for 7% of shipments, followed by Cambricon at 5%, Kunlunxin at 4% and Hygon at 3%. Nine of the 11 Chinese suppliers tracked by IDC increased shipments during the period. [Reuters]

report.summary: Nvidia's China data-center AI chip share fell to 34% in H1 2026 as Huawei climbed to 28%, signaling rapid domestic substitution under US export controls.
report.background: Nvidia has dominated AI accelerators globally, but successive rounds of US export restrictions since 2022 have repeatedly narrowed what it can legally sell into China — from the A100/H100 to the downgraded A800/H800 and later H20. Each tightening pushed Chinese cloud providers and labs toward domestic silicon, and Beijing reinforced that shift with procurement guidance favoring local chips and state-backed funding for foundries and chip designers. Huawei's Ascend line, built on its own CANN software stack, became the default alternative, while Alibaba, Cambricon, Kunlunxin (Baidu) and Hygon scaled their own accelerators. The result is a market that is still large but increasingly served by local vendors, with supply certainty and policy support mattering as much as raw performance per chip.
key_points: Nvidia's China AI accelerator share fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, down sharply from the near-monopoly position it held before export controls. It shipped 678,000 units in the period, a 44% year-on-year decline, showing that restrictions, not demand, are now the binding constraint on its China business.

Huawei reached 28% share on 572,000 Ascend shipments, roughly double its volume a year earlier. That makes it the clear number-two supplier and the default domestic option for Chinese clouds, telcos and state-linked AI projects that need predictable supply.

The long tail is consolidating into a real ecosystem: Alibaba's T-Head took 7%, Cambricon 5%, Kunlunxin 4% and Hygon 3%. Nine of the eleven Chinese suppliers tracked by IDC grew shipments, meaning this is broad-based expansion, not a single-company story.

The shift is structural rather than cyclical. Chinese buyers are standardizing on domestic chips and software stacks for training and inference, which locks in vendor relationships and makes it harder for Nvidia to win back share even if export rules were loosened.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is the clearest evidence yet that export controls are accelerating a bifurcated global compute market rather than slowing China's AI progress. Nvidia loses revenue and, more importantly, ecosystem gravity in the world's second-largest AI market, while Huawei becomes a genuine platform vendor whose CANN stack competes with CUDA in at least one major region. For developers, the practical cost is porting work: code, kernels and tooling written for CUDA increasingly need parallel support for Ascend and other domestic accelerators, and cross-platform frameworks gain value. For regular users, expect Chinese AI products to keep improving on domestic silicon while global models face compute constraints; pricing and availability of AI services may diverge more between regions.
report.tools: To follow this shift, watch Huawei's CANN toolkit and MindSpore framework, plus Ascend-targeting backends in vLLM and SGLang for inference. PaddlePaddle and OneFlow support domestic accelerators natively, and llama.cpp-style projects are adding non-CUDA backends. For benchmarking, MLPerf-style comparisons and the open-source Ascend ModelZoo are useful starting points if you want to test portability across Nvidia and Huawei hardware.
